name: github work-item unregistered REST collector
$limitation: This plan covers REST repository identity, selection, bounded traversal, optional-degradation markers, request evidence, and retry-stable semantic rows. PR GraphQL social data, effects, readback/recovery, watermark advancement, alias activation, and route readiness remain later stack layers.

mutations.rationale: the work-item rows must follow the API full_name used by the active Python repository model after a rename, not remain keyed to stale planner input
GitHub's issues endpoint includes PR stubs, which must be excluded so they cannot be fetched and normalized a second time as issues
GitHub has no issues-list active_until parameter, so the collector's client-side comparison is the only barrier against ingesting future-window issues
best-effort provider errors do not authorize accepting a known truncated milestone inventory as complete
a swallowed milestone request failure must not become indistinguishable from a successful empty milestone list
issue events drive status and reopen facts, so a failed traversal cannot be normalized as an event-free successful issue
a detail response for a different PR number must never be attached to the selected GraphQL target
explicit work-item claim options must override defaults so disabled issues, PRs, comments, and milestones do not issue provider requests
provider usage evidence must count actual wire attempts, including HTTP retries, rather than only successful logical pages
the 500-comment and 1000-event iterator limits must stop on the exact item without spending or depending on one extra provider page

GitHub rate limits carry retry scheduling semantics and must propagate instead of becoming best-effort incompleteness. Under the ratified optional-data contract this clause is what keeps a rate limit OUT of the continue-and-record path, so the composed route boundary is proved too, not just the collector.

the REST caller must preserve the active Python event limit of exactly 1000 per issue rather than merely exercising generic item-limited pagination

the typed collector options must retain the planner-frozen comments_limit value instead of accepting it and then silently discarding it
a later GitHub page failure must return earlier decoded pages so optional Python-compatible collectors can retain already observed rows while marking typed degradation
successfully decoded milestone pages remain valid observations when a later optional page fails and must be emitted beside the typed incomplete marker

legacy documented environment controls must be snapshotted once into durable config and dataset options before Go can own the claim
an explicit persisted comments_limit must win over the legacy environment value at every durable snapshot boundary
an unrelated PATCH must seed missing legacy SyncConfiguration controls from the repaired work-items dataset before consulting a changed process environment
a partial runtime PATCH must seed omitted controls from the repaired integration snapshot before consulting a changed process environment while explicit PATCH fields still win
